title: Novena for Expectant Parents
kicker: 9 days of hope for parents and their baby
card: For parents expecting a baby: 9 days asking for a safe pregnancy and birth, the baby’s health, and peace and strength for the parents.
ogDescription: 9 days of prayer for expectant parents and their baby, through Our Lady, St. Gerard, St. Elizabeth and St. Joseph.
description: A 9-day Catholic novena for expectant parents and their baby, through Our Lady of the Visitation, St. Gerard Majella, St. Elizabeth and St. Joseph.

epigraph.text: You formed my inmost being; / you knit me in my mother’s womb.

closingVerse.text: The LORD bless you and keep you! / The LORD let his face shine upon you, and be gracious to you! / The LORD look upon you kindly and give you peace!

saints.name: St. Gerard Majella
saints.bio: Tailor’s son from southern Italy, turned away by the Capuchins for poor health, who became a Redemptorist lay brother. Remembered for his charity and wonders, he died at 29.
saints.alt: Engraving: St. Gerard Majella holding a crucifix, from a 19th-century Life of the saint
saints.openingRole: friend of mothers and their children

saints.name: St. Elizabeth
saints.bio: Wife of the priest Zechariah; for many years the couple had no child. When Mary visited her, the baby in her womb leaped for joy, and she gave birth to John the Baptist.
saints.alt: Painting: St. Elizabeth embracing Mary at the Visitation, by Mariotto Albertinelli

saints.name: St. Joseph
saints.bio: Husband of Mary and foster father of Jesus, who took Mary into his home, brought her safely to Bethlehem and protected the Child and His mother on the flight into Egypt.
saints.alt: Painting: St. Joseph holding the Infant Jesus, by Guido Reni
saints.openingRole: guardian of Mary and her Child

openingPrayer: Heavenly Father, Giver of every life, You know N. and the child they are waiting for: their joy, their hopes and their worries. We place this pregnancy in Your hands. Keep mother and child safe, give this little one health and strength, and, whatever lies ahead, prepare N. to welcome the gift You are entrusting to them. Today we ask Our Lady of the Visitation; St. Gerard Majella, friend of mothers and their children; St. Elizabeth, who waited long and rejoiced; and St. Joseph, guardian of Mary and her Child, to join their prayers with ours, through Christ our Lord.
closingPrayer: Lord Jesus, once carried beneath Your mother’s heart, bless N. and the child they are waiting for. Keep them safe in Your love, give them peace in every season of waiting, and let Your holy will be done.

tips.p: One person leads each part; all respond pray for us and Amen, and say the closing prayers together. The prayers say “we”; if you pray alone, say “I”.

If you can, go to Confession and attend Mass during these 9 days, and ask a priest or deacon for the Church’s blessing of parents before childbirth. Pair prayer with good care: checkups, rest and help from others (Day 3). A medal is a sign of prayer, not a charm. At “N.”, say the parents’ names, or “me” or “us” if you pray for yourself.

If you face a hard diagnosis, a high-risk pregnancy or a loss, you are not alone, and it is never a sign that you prayed too little (Day 8). Lean on your doctor and your parish. If a newborn is in danger of death, ask for Baptism at once; in an emergency, anyone may baptize.

intentionPlaceholder: Write the parents’ names, the baby’s due date, and the graces you ask.
credits: Images: Mariotto Albertinelli, The Visitation, 1503, Uffizi, Florence · St. Gerard Majella, engraving, 1890s · Guido Reni, St Joseph with the Infant Jesus, c. 1635, Hermitage. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

days.title: Bringing Our Hopes & Fears
days.verse: when I am afraid, / in you I place my trust.
days.refl: The psalmist does not claim that he is never afraid. He tells us what he does with his fear: he places his trust in God. Waiting for a child brings joy, and it can bring fear too: about the baby’s health, the birth, money, and whether we will be good parents. God does not ask us to hide those worries. He invites us to bring them to Him just as they are. So we begin these nine days by placing every hope and every fear in His hands.
days.more: Even the holiest people in Scripture were stirred by new life. When the angel greeted Mary, she was greatly troubled, and he told her not to be afraid (Luke 1:29–30). Elizabeth, after years of waiting, went into seclusion for five months once she had conceived (Luke 1:24). God met each of them with patience. We can be honest with Him too, about our excitement, our nerves and anything else on our hearts.
days.prayer: Heavenly Father, You know N. and the child they are waiting for, and You know every hope and fear in their hearts. We bring them all to You now. As You spoke peace to Mary, speak peace to N. today. Through the prayers of Our Lady of the Visitation, St. Gerard, St. Elizabeth and St. Joseph, calm their worries, strengthen their trust, and help them take this pregnancy one day at a time.
days.step: Write down one hope and one worry about this pregnancy, and offer both to God in a short prayer.

days.title: Known & Loved Before Birth
days.verse: Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, / before you were born I dedicated you, / a prophet to the nations I appointed you.
days.refl: God told the young Jeremiah that He knew him before He formed him in the womb. The same is true of the child on the way. Before anyone has seen this little face, God already knows and loves this child, and has a purpose for their life. A pregnancy is not only something to get through; it is the hidden beginning of a person whom God calls by name. Today we thank Him for this new life, already precious in His eyes.
days.more: The Church teaches that every human life must be respected and protected from the moment of conception (CCC 2270). God’s plans are often surprising. St. Gerard Majella was a frail tailor’s son, turned away by the Capuchins because of his health, yet he became a Redemptorist brother whose kindness is still remembered nearly three centuries later. Whatever lies ahead, this child’s worth will never depend on strength or success.
days.prayer: Lord God, You are forming this child in secret, and You know them by name. We thank You for the gift of this new life, loved by You before anyone has seen their face. Through the prayers of St. Gerard, St. Elizabeth and St. Joseph, protect this little one as they grow, and help N. to welcome their child as a gift from You, whatever their needs and whatever Your plan for their life.
days.step: Thank God today for this child, by name or simply as “little one,” and pray one Hail Mary for them.

days.title: No One Waits Alone
days.verse: During those days Mary set out and traveled to the hill country in haste to a town of Judah, where she entered the house of Zechariah and greeted Elizabeth.
days.refl: As soon as Mary learned that her relative Elizabeth was expecting, she hurried to be with her. Two women, each carrying a child, met in a simple house and shared their joy. No one should carry a pregnancy alone. Parents need people who listen, help and pray, and who notice when they are tired. Today we thank God for everyone who surrounds N. with care, and we ask Him to send support wherever it is missing.
days.more: When Mary greeted her, the baby in Elizabeth’s womb leaped, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit (Luke 1:41). Then Mary stayed with her about three months (Luke 1:56). St. Elizabeth knew what it meant to wait: for many years she and Zechariah had no child. Now her joy was shared, and so was the work of those last months. Love often looks like that: practical, patient and present.
days.prayer: Loving Father, as Mary hurried to be with Elizabeth, surround N. with people who will help and encourage them. Bless their families and friends, and everyone who will share in the work of these months. Through the prayers of Our Lady of the Visitation and St. Elizabeth, may N. never feel alone, and may the joy of this child, like the joy of John leaping in his mother’s womb, be shared by many.
days.step: Offer the parents one practical help today, such as a meal, an errand or a ride; if you are expecting, accept one offer of help.

days.title: A Father’s Courage
days.verse: Such was his intention when, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, “Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary your wife into your home. For it is through the holy Spirit that this child has been conceived in her. She will bear a son and you are to name him Jesus, because he will save his people from their sins.”
days.refl: Joseph faced an uncertain future, and God spoke to him the words every parent needs to hear: do not be afraid. Joseph took Mary into his home and cared for her and the Child she carried. Fathers, and all who stand beside an expectant mother, have a holy part to play. Their patience, protection and steady love matter more than they may realize. Today we pray that God will make every father and every support person strong, gentle and faithful.
days.more: St. Joseph never speaks a word in the Gospels, yet his actions say a great deal. He made the long journey to Bethlehem with Mary and stayed beside her when there was no room for them in the inn (Luke 2:4–7). Later he rose in the night and took the Child and His mother to safety in Egypt (Matthew 2:13–14). Quiet faithfulness is a powerful kind of love.
days.prayer: Lord God, You entrusted Mary and the Child she carried to the care of St. Joseph. Give every father, and everyone who supports this pregnancy, a share in his courage and tenderness. Free them from fear, and help them provide and protect with wisdom. Where a mother waits without the child’s father beside her, be her strength and send her faithful help. Through the prayers of St. Joseph, St. Gerard and St. Elizabeth, make the home of N. a place where this child will always know Your love.
days.step: If you support the mother, lighten her load in one way today; if you are the mother, accept one offer of help and pray for those who stand by you.

days.title: Peace in the Waiting
days.verse: Have no anxiety at all, but in everything, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, make your requests known to God. Then the peace of God that surpasses all understanding will guard your hearts and minds in Christ Jesus.
days.refl: Pregnancy is full of waiting: for the next checkup, for test results, for the first kick, for the day labor begins. Waiting can stir up anxiety, especially at night. St. Paul does not scold the anxious. He shows them a way: bring every request to God, with thanks for what He has already given. Then His peace guards our hearts and minds, a peace that does not depend on knowing everything that lies ahead.
days.more: St. Gerard Majella knew how to wait in peace. When he was falsely accused of a grave sin, he made no defense and accepted the penance placed on him. In time his accuser took back her words, and his name was cleared. Gerard trusted that God saw everything. We may not know the result of a test or the day of the birth, but we know the One who holds them.
days.prayer: Lord Jesus, You know how long the days of waiting can feel. Calm the anxious thoughts of N., especially in the night and before every checkup. Teach them to bring each worry to You with thanks, and guard their hearts and minds with Your peace. Through the prayers of St. Gerard, who trusted You in silence, and of St. Elizabeth and St. Joseph, help N. to rest in Your care, one day at a time.
days.step: Whenever worry rises today, pray slowly, “Jesus, I trust in You,” and name one thing you are thankful for.

days.title: Skill for Doctors & Midwives
days.verse: The midwives, however, feared God; they did not do as the king of Egypt had ordered them, but let the boys live.
days.refl: The Hebrew midwives Shiphrah and Puah protected newborn boys at great risk, because they feared God more than Pharaoh. Today, too, God works through those who care for mothers and babies: obstetricians, midwives, nurses and pediatricians. Their knowledge, attention and steady hands can make all the difference. Faith and good medical care go together. So we pray for everyone who will look after this mother and child, and ask God to guide them in every decision.
days.more: St. Gianna Beretta Molla, canonized in 2004, knew this work from the inside. An Italian doctor, she opened a clinic in the town of Mesero in 1950 and went on to specialize in pediatrics. She married Pietro Molla in 1955 and became the mother of four children. She is honored today as a patron of mothers, doctors and unborn children. We can ask her prayers for everyone who cares for this mother and child.
days.prayer: Lord, Giver of life, bless the doctors, midwives, nurses and all who care for N. and their child. Give them wisdom in every decision, skill in every procedure, and gentleness in every word. Like the faithful midwives of Egypt, may they always protect life with courage. Through the prayers of St. Gerard, St. Elizabeth and St. Joseph, guide their minds and hands, and make their work an instrument of Your care.
days.step: Pray by name for the doctor or midwife caring for this pregnancy, and thank a health worker you know this week.

days.title: A Safe Delivery
days.verse: When a woman is in labor, she is in anguish because her hour has arrived; but when she has given birth to a child, she no longer remembers the pain because of her joy that a child has been born into the world.
days.refl: Jesus Himself spoke about labor. He did not pretend it is easy: there is pain, and there is a moment when the hour arrives. But He also spoke of the joy that follows, when a child has been born into the world. Today we pray for the day of birth: for the mother’s strength and safety, for the baby’s safe arrival, and for calm hearts in everyone who will be there. Whatever that day brings, Christ will be present.
days.more: St. Gerard Majella is remembered as the mothers’ saint because of a story told since his time. A few months before he died, he dropped his handkerchief at a family’s home and told the girl who returned it to keep it, because one day it would be of use to her. Years later, in danger during childbirth, she asked for it and delivered safely. We ask his prayers in trust, not as a charm.
days.prayer: Lord Jesus, You told us that anguish gives way to joy when a child has been born into the world. When the hour of birth comes, give the mother strength, protect mother and child, and bring them safely through. Bless everyone present at the birth with calm and skill. Through the prayers of St. Gerard, friend of mothers, and of St. Elizabeth and St. Joseph, let this birth be wrapped in Your peace and followed by deep joy.
days.step: Pray one Hail Mary for the day of birth, asking Our Lady to be with mother and child in that hour.

days.title: When the Road Is Hard
days.verse: The LORD is close to the brokenhearted, / saves those whose spirit is crushed.
days.refl: Not every pregnancy goes as hoped. Some parents hear a hard diagnosis, face bed rest or a high-risk birth, or carry the grief of a baby lost before. The psalm does not promise that hearts will never break. It promises that the Lord is close when they do. If this is your road, you are not being punished, and it is never a sign that you prayed too little. God is close to you, and no child is ever forgotten by Him.
days.more: For parents who have lost a child before birth, the Church entrusts these little ones to the mercy of God, who desires that all be saved, and allows us to hope for their salvation (CCC 1261). She offers funeral rites for these children and a blessing for grieving parents. St. Joseph knew fear and uncertainty, and St. Elizabeth knew years of sorrow. They stand with every parent who is hurting.
days.prayer: Lord, You are close to the brokenhearted. If this pregnancy brings difficult news or danger, stay close to N. and give them courage for each decision. Comfort every parent who has lost a child, and hold their little ones in Your mercy. Through the prayers of Our Lady of the Visitation, St. Elizabeth, St. Joseph and St. Gerard, give N. Your strength in their weakness, and a peace that holds even when answers are hard.
days.step: Pray today for parents facing a difficult pregnancy or the loss of a child, and if you know one, send them a short message of love.

days.title: Gratitude & Trust in God’s Will
days.verse: Mary said, “Behold, I am the handmaid of the Lord. May it be done to me according to your word.” Then the angel departed from her.
days.refl: Mary did not know everything that lay ahead when she said yes. She trusted the God who had spoken to her, and placed her whole future in His hands. We end these nine days in the same spirit: giving thanks for the gift of this child, and entrusting the pregnancy, the birth and every day after it to God’s loving will. With Our Lady, St. Gerard, St. Elizabeth and St. Joseph, we place N. and their little one in the hands of a faithful Father.
days.more: When Elizabeth gave birth, her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord had shown his great mercy toward her, and they rejoiced with her (Luke 1:58). Looking back over these nine days, we may notice small graces: a reassuring checkup, a kind word, a calmer heart, a friend who helped. Trusting God’s will does not mean we stop asking. It means we keep praying in peace, knowing this child is loved.
days.prayer: Lord, on this ninth day we thank You for the gift of life and for every grace, seen and unseen, that You have given N. and their child. Thank you, Our Lady of the Visitation, St. Gerard, St. Elizabeth and St. Joseph, for carrying our prayers to Jesus. With Mary we say, “May it be done,” and we entrust this pregnancy, this birth and this child’s whole life to Your loving will.
days.step: Write down three graces you noticed during these nine days, and thank God for them together.

printClosing: The LORD bless you and keep you! The LORD let his face shine upon you, and be gracious to you!
The LORD look upon you kindly and give you peace!
